title_en: Costco Has Dropped the Cost of Digital Copies of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on Nintendo Switch 2 to $55 for Members
summary_en: Costco members can grab a digital copy of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on Switch 2 for $54.99 from the retailer, saving $5 compared to paying its digital list price.
body_en:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is officially out in the world (and we really loved it ). If you don't have a copy yet for your Nintendo Switch 2 and are dying to jump in, Costco can help you out as it's currently offering digital copies for $54.99 .
There's a catch, though: this offer is only available to Costco members. But if that's you, then you can score a nice little $5 discount on this game right after launch day. Just make sure you're logged into your account before you head to checkout so you can take advantage of this offer while it's still available.
No matter if you have fond memories of the original or if it's your first time playing, you're in for a wonderful time with this remake if you decide to buy it. IGN's Logan Plant had heaps of praise for it in his 9/10 review , writing that "Nintendo skillfully melds the world and dungeon design of classic Zeldas with the movement and presentation of its more recent games, creating both a beautiful retelling of a legend and a rich adventure that stands on its own."
If you're a Costco member, this is a nice way to save a little cash on this brand new launch. And if you're on the hunt for more video game discounts right now, you're in luck: Early Black Friday deals are already starting to drop, with Best Buy and Target both launching their own early sales ahead of the weekend.
The whole month of November is full of different sale events from various retailers in the lead-up to Black Friday, though. If you're curious when you'll be able to find some more game deals during this seasonal sale, check out our rundown of sale dates and what to expect to learn more about what retailer's plans are for this year.
Hannah Hoolihan is a freelancer who writes with the commerce team here at IGN.
